note.explanation: Noble elements are the elements in group 18. They exist as single atoms, have very low boiling points and are mostly unreactive because their outer electron shells are complete. For example, helium has the configuration s², while neon has s²p⁶.
examples: Helium is a noble element in group 18.
Neon has a complete outer shell with the configuration s²p⁶.
note.checkAnswer: Noble elements are mostly unreactive because their outer shells are complete.
note.simple: Noble gases are single atoms with full outer shells, so they hardly react.
note.checkQuestion: Why do noble elements show very little chemical reactivity?
note.title: Properties of Noble Gases
steps: Identify noble elements as group 18 elements.
Check that they exist as single atoms.
Recall that their outer shells are complete, except helium has s².
Link the complete outer shell to very little chemical reactivity.
note.answer: Noble elements are group 18 elements; they are monoatomic gases with very low boiling points and very little chemical reactivity.

If asked for a property of noble elements, give the precise term monoatomic rather than saying only that they are gases.

explain.title: Where noble elements are found
explain.body: Elements present in group 18 of the modern periodic table are called noble elements.

explain.title: How they exist
explain.body: All noble elements are monoatomic gases having very low boiling points, Helium (He), Neon (Ne) Argon (Ar), Krypton (Kr), Xenone (Xe) and Radon (Ra). Monoatomic means each gas exists as single atoms.

explain.title: Their outer electrons
explain.body: All these gases have eight electrons (s²p⁶) in their outermost shells except He which has s² electronic configuration.

explain.title: Why they hardly react
explain.body: Since their outer shells are complete, they show very little chemical reactivity.

mistakes: Do not say that helium has s²p⁶; the section gives helium's configuration as s².
Do not confuse monoatomic with diatomic: noble elements exist as single atoms.
Do not say noble elements are completely unable to react; the section says they show very little chemical reactivity.
When asked why they are unreactive, give the reason: their outer shells are complete.
